persona: Absolute beginner seeking a relaxed lo-fi sketch
study_type: Independent simulated beginner evaluation; not a human participant

protocol.app_interaction: Mouse only: click, double-click, drag; screenshots for observation
lab_limits: Null audio output: no listening or subjective sonic-quality claims
Actual native test VST3 Rill Lab Sine; does not validate third-party plug-ins
Stock demo audio was supplied by the app

outcome.music_description: Repeated eight-note sine melody over the stock Circuit rhythm audio, with both final clips trimmed at 30 seconds. No audible musical assessment was possible.

rating_scale: Higher is more of the named quality; high confusion is worse. Ratings are simulated impressions of observed workflow, not benchmarks.

rating_reasons.easy_to_use: Could create and export the audio+MIDI piece without outside workflow instructions. Mouse precision and selection behavior added recovery steps.
rating_reasons.how_cool_it_looks: Consistent restrained dark palette, clear waveform and note displays, readable labels. Modal blur obscures the context while menus are open.
rating_reasons.how_fast_it_is: Actions generally responded immediately, drawing and duplication felt direct, and the 30-second render completed in seconds. Software OpenGL/null audio limits performance generalization.
rating_reasons.how_confusing_it_is: Pencil state carried from piano roll into arranger; clicking an already-selected clip retained the whole selection; numeric timing fields had no visible mouse controls.
rating_reasons.feature_completeness: Core audio, VST3 MIDI, editing, looping, save and WAV/MIDI export worked. Mouse-only exact values and naming remain weaker; preset/instrument richness was not assessable with one test instrument.

findings.problem: Duration and loop-end numeric editors expose text editing but no visible +/- or mouse adjustment affordance.
findings.observed: Clicked Properties Duration and Range End; both became text inputs. Reaching exact30 required repeated trims and discovery of Fit selection.
findings.recommendation: Provide accessible increment/decrement controls and a clear unit selector for beats/bars/seconds, with immediate duration feedback.

findings.problem: Tool mode persists from piano-roll note drawing into arranger unexpectedly.
findings.observed: Returned with Pencil active; attempted clip-edge trim did not change length. Switched Select and retried successfully.
findings.recommendation: Remember tool per editor or explicitly announce the active tool on return; ensure an edge hover explains resize availability.

findings.problem: Clicking a selected clip retains a multiple-clip selection, so Fit selection zoomed all clips when one was intended.
findings.observed: Clicked final MIDI clip after Select all, chose Fit selection, and all clips enlarged. Right-click Select only this clip resolved it.
findings.recommendation: Make selection count visible and make a plain click select only the clicked clip when no drag follows, while preserving group drag behavior.

findings.problem: Precise snap timing is difficult when a beat occupies only a few pixels; the initial 30-second trim landed at30.134s.
findings.observed: Initial export showed0:30.134; fit final clips then trim achieved0:30.000.
findings.recommendation: Show start/end/duration during trim, and offer Fit selection near main Fit or a contextual zoom action.

positive_findings: The empty-lane Double-click for MIDI hint directly enabled instrument creation.
Instrument chooser clearly exposed format VST3 and an Assign instrument action.
Pencil tool explained drag to set note length, and the clip grew as notes were drawn beyond its initial end.
Context menus exposed Duplicate, Loop selection, and Select only this clip without requiring keyboard shortcuts.
Save and export had useful default names, allowing mouse-only completion.
WAV export displayed exact duration and a clear success toast.
